_comment: Per-resident Fish Audio voices. Read by serve.py; keys starting with '_'
are documentation and are ignored. Each entry is {id, speed, volume} —
'id' is the Fish reference_id (fish.audio/m/<id>), 'speed' is a prosody
multiplier (>1 faster, <1 slower), 'volume' is a dB offset.
HOW THESE WERE CHOSEN (2026-08-22). The catalogue was queried via
GET https://api.fish.audio/model?language=hi — there are ~968 public
community voices whose reference audio is native Hindi. Candidates were
shortlisted on Fish's own tags (gender/age/timbre) plus its
quality.quality_passed flag, then scored objectively: each candidate
spoke the same ROMANIZED Hindi line, the audio was fed back through
Fish ASR (POST /v1/asr), and the transcript was compared against the
known Devanagari ground truth. Score = character similarity; the
winners are recorded in '_sim' below. Re-run that round trip before
swapping any voice — tags alone are not a reliable guide.
WHY THIS WORKS AT ALL: the game sends Latin-script Hindi ('mujhe teen
kele chahiye'), never Devanagari. Model s2.1-pro auto-detects language
from the text and reads romanized Hindi AS Hindi — verified, ASR
returns language_code 'hi' for every voice below. Do not downgrade to
s1/s2 without re-running the check.
KNOWN LIMITATIONS — read before 'fixing' these:
1. lucia is 9 years old and there is NO native-Hindi child voice in the
catalogue (only 2 models are tagged 'child' and both are English).
The English child voices were tested and they FAIL on Hindi: one
scored 0.712, and 'Young Female Girl Child' scored 0.984 on one line
then emitted fluent FINNISH on the next. So lucia uses a native
Hindi young-female voice sped up slightly. She reads as a bright
young woman, not a child. This is the honest ceiling today.
2. Fish prosody accepts only 'speed' and 'volume'. A 'pitch' field is
accepted but has no measurable effect (tested: output stayed inside
the run-to-run noise band), so pitch cannot be used to age voices
up or down. Character separation comes from timbre + speed only.
3. These are community-uploaded models. They can be deleted or taken
down by their authors; serve.py logs a clear error and falls back to
the default voice if an id stops resolving.
4. Deliberately avoided: clones of real public figures (politicians,
actors, cricketers) and franchise cartoon characters, both of which
are plentiful in this catalogue and neither of which belongs in a
shipped game.

coach._why: Marco speaks ENGLISH, not Hindi. Male/middle-aged, tagged warm+calm+gentle+measured — the coach read. 51.8k uses.

rosa._why: Female 58, warm. Native hi, quality_passed, tagged warm+smooth+calm+friendly. Best-scoring warm female.

pilar._why: Female 41, quick and bright. Native hi, quality_passed, tagged energetic+expressive+cheerful. Top Hindi score of the female candidates.

tomas._why: Male 44, loud and low. Native hi, tagged deep+low+energetic+authoritative. Volume lifted to make him carry.

carmen._why: Female 79. One of only 21 native-Hindi voices tagged female+old; tagged soft+warm+calm+relaxed. Slowed for age.

miguel._why: Male 27, laid-back. Native hi, quality_passed, tagged smooth+calm+friendly+conversational.

lucia._why: Girl, 9 — SEE LIMITATION 1. Best available compromise: native Hindi, tagged female+young+energetic+enthusiastic, 2.3k uses, scored 0.976-0.984 across two lines. Sped up for childlike energy, but this is a young woman's timbre.

padre._why: Male 66, slow and gentle. Native hi, quality_passed, tagged old+calm+measured+low. Slowed hard for the unhurried priest read.
